chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Sy Oliver, Willie Smith and Wilcox on the team and gigs
summary: Crawford says Sy was too delicate for sports, and describes Wilcox's piano playing and the band's gigs.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did Sy Oliver play on the team?
Oh, Sy was too delicate. He talked a lot. His hands and fingers like that --

Willie played, good shortstop, Wilcox, [his name was.] You know, he was a lefthanded piano player. I don't see how he got that speed and drive, but up here -- trebles, right hand, but he was actually a left handed piano player.

When I first heard him at Fisk University, that guy excited me, man, play an ad lib first chorus, just throwing those big chords in there and tintinabulating with his right hand. And then after that first chorus he'd stop, pause and then go into that stride, you know. Oh, he was a very impressive piano player.
And so when you all played other teams, I mean would you all spend -- like did you all stay together after you all would finish the baseball game and go do other things, or what did you do?
Go on gigs, whatever gigs were available. That's all. I never did anything in New York other than play drums, all I wanted to do. And so that's it. Go on a gig, that's all.
Make some meat and bread money.
